subject: Dedicated capacity: prioritized-queue guardrails and fallback request (Hanover AI)
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@hanover.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@hanover.ai>
Date: 2026-10-05T14:02:00Z
Subject: Dedicated capacity: queue behavior & prioritized fallback for mixed jobs

Karthik —

Thanks for the quick call today. As discussed, Hanover AI is preparing to sign a 12‑month reserved GPU commitment and we need a formal agreement on queueing behavior and fallback policies that preserve our low‑latency inference lanes during nightly batch windows. Main asks: 

- A throughput guarantee for our reserved pool (baseline tokens/sec) with a clear measurement window.
- Controlled preemption rules: we need assurance that real‑time lanes (<50ms P95) aren’t evicted for non‑urgent batch jobs except under documented emergency conditions.
- A fallback plan if capacity pressure requires routing to shared instances — what model variants will be used and how will latency/cost be communicated to us?
- An ops/runbook and escalation path for incidents that degrade tail latency for our low‑latency customers.

I attached an expected load matrix (hourly QPS mix) and a short note on our SLOs. Procurement will need a runbook and an exception clause in the SOW that limits preemption during our peak windows or offers credits if thresholds are crossed.

Can Redwood provide a draft runbook and a proposed carve‑out/credit structure we can take to our legal team? We aim to execute by Oct 20 to hit our product launch.

Appreciate it —
Sanjay
VP Product, Hanover AI
--- attachment: HAN-expected-load-matrix.csv (csv) ---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@hanover.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: queue behavior & prioritized fallback for mixed jobs

Sanjay —

Thanks for the clear summary and the load matrix. I ran this by our capacity and runtime teams; below is an initial, pragmatic approach we can offer for the SOW and runbook (we'll formalize in the SOW PDF and runbook doc):

1) Baseline guarantee: we can commit a sustained throughput baseline measured as a 1‑hour sliding window (tokens/sec) for the reserved pool. If utilization falls below the committed baseline across that window due to infra issues, we will issue service credits equivalent to agreed token unit value.

2) Priority lanes: we will carve two logical lanes inside your reserved pool — a low‑latency lane (70% of pool capacity configurable) for inference requests with P95 target <50ms and a background lane for batch jobs. Background jobs will be rate limited and admitted only to spare capacity.

3) Preemption rules: preemption of low‑latency lanes will be limited to declared emergency events (hardware failure, region outage). Non‑emergency preemption will fall back to soft‑degradation policies (rate limiting, micro‑queuing) rather than eviction. If we must route low‑latency traffic to shared hosts, we'll only do so to pre‑quantized compatible variants and will attach a live note in the Console with expected latency delta and cost delta.

4) Fallback and observability: automatic fallback to a compatible model variant + telemetry hooks for per‑request latency flags. We'll provide a runnable ops playbook (attached as capacity-runbook-v1.md) that includes: hit counters, escalation matrix, runbook steps, and rollback criteria.

5) Credits & remedies: proposed credit band tied to minutes of degraded P95 beyond agreed thresholds per month. Example: if P95 exceeds 50ms for >60 minutes/month, credit = X% of monthly commitment. We'll put concrete numbers in the SOW draft.

Next step: Marissa will coordinate a two‑hour technical + procurement session with your team to lock numbers and workflow. Ben will draft proposed credit wording for procurement to review. If this outline looks right to you, we'll produce the SOW PDF and runbook and circulate for signatures.

I've attached the initial runbook and will add the SOW draft after the internal review.

—Karthik
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
--- attachment: capacity-runbook-v1.md (markdown) ---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T11:05:00Z
Subject: Fw: Dedicated capacity: queue behavior & prioritized fallback for mixed jobs

Team —

Looping you in on Hanover's ask (see original below). Quick notes for coordination before we hand this to legal/procurement: 

- Marissa: schedule the technical + procurement alignment for next week (90–120 mins). Hanover wants to sign by Oct 20; we should push for a final SOW by Oct 15.
- Ben: propose credit bands — I suggest a 0.5–2% monthly credit ladder depending on minutes of P95 degradation; start with conservative numbers so procurement has room to negotiate.
- Lauren: procurement/legal, we'll need a short exception clause that: (a) defines emergency preemption; (b) specifies the measurement window (1h sliding) and telemetry sources (Console logs + token counters); and (c) ties credits to measured minutes. Also need language on acceptable fallback model families.

Operational constraints from infra: our runtime can reserve logical lanes but not strict physical isolation unless they take a node‑level reservation at higher commit levels. If Hanover needs hard physical isolation for peak windows, call that out — that'll change pricing.

I'll review Ben's credit wording once you have the draft. I've pasted Sanjay's original message below for context.

—Karthik
(On behalf of Hanover thread)

Sanjay / Procurement —

Thanks again for the call and the load matrix. Per Karthik's outline, attached is a first‑pass SOW that includes: baseline throughput definition, priority‑lane carve (70% low‑latency by default), preemption exceptions, monitoring hooks, and a credit schedule tied to minutes of P95 breach. Key operational points included in the SOW:

- Measurement: P95 measured at the Console edge per 1‑hour sliding window, aggregated by model route.
- Priority lane config: configurable percentage (default 70%) with an option to increase at higher commit tiers.
- Fallback behavior: automatic routing to compatible quantized variants with console banner and alert to your oncall; worst‑case expected P95 delta documented in the runbook.
- Credits: credit ladder (examples) in section 6; Ben will update numeric bands by EOD.

Next steps: if you confirm this approach we will: (1) update numeric thresholds and credit percentages after Monday's technical alignment, (2) produce the SOW PDF for signature, and (3) finalize the runbook. Signing link (DocuSign) will be provided once procurement confirms wording.
